evidence: src/domain/errors.ts: DomainError, with ValidationError, NotFoundError and ConflictError as subclasses, is the single error abstraction used throughout the module
src/domain/task.ts: createTask throws ValidationError and markTaskDone throws ConflictError, so task failures use the module's error types
src/domain/project.ts: createProject throws ValidationError("Project name is required")
src/domain/user.ts: createUser throws ValidationError("User name is required"), mirroring createProject; this is a minor per-entity invariant, not duplication of a shared rule
src/domain/repositories.ts: UserRepository, ProjectRepository and TaskRepository reference User, Project and Task, and TaskFilter reuses TaskStatus from task.ts instead of redefining it
src/domain/task.ts: TASK_STATUSES, TaskStatus and isTaskStatus are the only definition of task status values
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The src/domain module is one cohesive domain model for task management. It contains entity types with their factories and transitions (project.ts, user.ts, task.ts), a shared error hierarchy (errors.ts) and repository ports (repositories.ts). All validation and conflict failures go through the module's own DomainError subclasses, not plain Error. The repository ports reuse the entity types and TaskStatus instead of redefining them. Task status invariants exist only in task.ts. The only near-duplication is the trimmed, non-empty name check in createProject and createUser. That is a small per-entity invariant, not a shared rule that has been misplaced, so it does not amount to a rubric violation.
